title: Lifting equal-degree fractions through a graded localized map
statement: Let k be a field and S=k[x_0,x_1] with its total-degree homogeneous submodules S_n. Let M and N be S-modules whose additive groups are internal direct sums of subgroups M_z and N_z for z in the integers. Assume S_n N_z is contained in N_(n+z) for every nonnegative n. Let g:M→N be S-linear and satisfy g(M_z)⊆N_z. Let f∈S_d for a nonnegative integer d. Localize at the powers T of f and let g_T:T^{-1}M→T^{-1}N be the induced map. If x∈T^{-1}N is an equal-degree fraction [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions] and lies in the range of g_T, then x has a preimage under g_T which is an equal-degree fraction in T^{-1}M. No injectivity, exactness, surjectivity, positive degree, or scalar compatibility of the source grading is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 01M7 (lemma-proj-sheaves), final functoriality paragraph; Algebra Section 00JM, homogeneous localization

proof.text: Choose decompositions of M and N from their internal direct sums. For an additive H:M→N with H(M_z)⊆N_(z+t), projection of H(a) onto degree z+t is H applied to the degree-z projection of a. To prove this, precompose both additive maps with the canonical source direct-sum map. On a generator in degree i=z both projections are the element itself; for i≠z both are zero, since i+t≠z+t. DirectSum.addHom_ext gives equality on the whole direct sum and its inverse gives the identity on M.

source.place: Lemma 01M7 (lemma-proj-sheaves), final functoriality paragraph; Algebra Section 00JM, homogeneous localization

proof.text: If f=0, the localization of N is subsingleton because T contains zero. The zero fraction 0/1 is an equal-degree preimage. Otherwise write x=b/f^m with b in degree n. Since f^m is nonzero, its total degree equals both n and d*m, hence n=d*m. Write an ordinary preimage as a/f^r. The equality of fractions is equivalent to f^l f^m g(a)=f^l f^r b for some l, or f^(l+m)g(a)=f^(l+r)b.

source.place: Lemma 01M7 (lemma-proj-sheaves), final functoriality paragraph; Algebra Section 00JM, homogeneous localization

proof.text: The additive map H(a)=f^(l+m)g(a) shifts degrees by d*(l+m), by the degree-preserving property of g and scalar compatibility in N. The right side f^(l+r)b lies in degree d*(l+r)+d*m=d*r+d*(l+m). Apply the projection identity in source degree d*r to get f^(l+m)g(a_(d*r))=f^(l+r)b. The fraction equality criterion with the same annihilating power f^l now proves g_T(a_(d*r)/f^r)=x. Its numerator and denominator both have degree d*r, so it is an equal-degree fraction.

theorem away_degreeZero_lift
    (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (M : Type v) (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N]
    [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) M] [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) N]
    (𝓜 : ℤ → AddSubgroup M) (𝓝 : ℤ → AddSubgroup N)
    (h𝓜 : DirectSum.IsInternal 𝓜) (h𝓝 : DirectSum.IsInternal 𝓝)
    (hsmulN : ∀ (n : ℕ) (z : ℤ) (a : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (y : N),
      a ∈ homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k n → y ∈ 𝓝 z → a • y ∈ 𝓝 (n + z))
    (f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (d : ℕ)
    (hf : f ∈ homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k d)
    (g : M →ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k] N)
    (hg : ∀ (z : ℤ) (y : M), y ∈ 𝓜 z → g y ∈ 𝓝 z)
    (x : LocalizedModule.Away f N)
    (hx : x ∈ degreeZeroFractions
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k n : Set (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)))
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝓝 n : Set N)) (Submonoid.powers f))
    (himage : x ∈ Set.range (IsLocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers f)
      (mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers f) M) (mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers f) N) g)) :
    ∃ y ∈ degreeZeroFractions
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k n : Set (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)))
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝓜 n : Set M)) (Submonoid.powers f),
      IsLocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers f)
        (mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers f) M) (mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers f) N) g y = x
